title: OpenAI Just Filed for Its IPO. SpaceX Goes Public Thursday. Anthropic Filed Last Week.
excerpt: Three trillion-dollar AI companies are racing to public markets in the same quarter. Perplexity's Aravind Srinivas says he is watching closely.
body:
OpenAI filed its confidential S-1 with the SEC on Monday, joining rival Anthropic and Elon Musk's SpaceX in what is shaping up to be the most consequential week for public markets since the dot-com era. If all three listings proceed as planned, 2026 will almost certainly shatter every IPO record in history.

"We recently submitted a confidential S-1," OpenAI said in a terse statement. "We expect it to leak so we're just announcing it."

The ChatGPT maker is targeting a valuation of up to $1 trillion, according to Reuters. It would join SpaceX — which goes public on Thursday at a $1.75 trillion valuation with a $75 billion offering — and Anthropic, which filed its own S-1 on June 1 after raising $65 billion at a $965 billion valuation.

https://x.com/sama/status/2064088940932641225

Together, these three companies could inject over $200 billion in new equity into public markets before autumn. Some bankers are already warning the capital surge could crowd out smaller deals for months.

## The Numbers Behind the Filing

OpenAI disclosed in March that ChatGPT has more than 900 million weekly active users and over 50 million paying subscribers. The company said it was generating $2 billion in monthly revenue — growing roughly four times faster than companies that defined the internet era, including Google and Meta.

But profitability remains distant. OpenAI has told investors it does not expect to turn a profit until 2030. It recently completed the largest funding round in Silicon Valley history — $122 billion from Amazon, Nvidia, SoftBank, and others — at an $840 billion post-money valuation.

The company is burning cash at a rate that would "dwarf any other public company in history," the Wall Street Journal reported.

## The Indian Connection

The AI IPO wave has a pronounced Indian diaspora dimension. Aravind Srinivas, the Indian-American CEO of Perplexity AI, told CNBC on Monday that his company plans to go public in 2028 regardless of how the OpenAI and Anthropic listings perform.

"I certainly think there will be ripple effects if they don't go well," Srinivas said. "The SpaceX IPO this week will definitely be a leading indicator."

Srinivas — who studied at IIT Madras before moving to the U.S. for his PhD at UC Berkeley — has built Perplexity into one of the most closely watched AI search startups. "By consistently holding 2028 as our earliest date, Perplexity has been able to build a healthy, high-growth business," said Chief Business Officer Dmitry Shevelenko.

The broader Indian tech ecosystem stands to be deeply affected by how public markets receive these AI giants. India's IT services firms — TCS, Infosys, Wipro, HCLTech — derive a significant share of revenue from building and integrating AI solutions for enterprise clients. A buoyant AI market lifts demand for their services; a crash would have the opposite effect. Wipro already slid 8.4% on Monday to a three-year low.

## ChatGPT's "Super App" Pivot

The filing comes as OpenAI scrambles to transform ChatGPT from a chatbot into a full-fledged platform. Internal plans, first reported by the Financial Times, envision a "super app" with integrated coding tools and AI agents capable of performing simultaneous tasks.

The pivot is partly defensive. Anthropic's Claude Code has emerged as the tool of choice for software developers, and its top-tier model Mythos is winning enterprise contracts for code review and vulnerability detection. OpenAI's competitive moat — once seemingly unassailable — has narrowed considerably.

"Chat is dead," one senior OpenAI employee told the Financial Times, describing the company's internal reorientation from conversational AI to agentic computing.

## What It Means for NRI Investors

For the millions of Indian-origin professionals in Silicon Valley and beyond, the AI IPO trifecta presents both opportunity and risk. SpaceX, OpenAI, and Anthropic are among the most sought-after pre-IPO allocations in history. Many NRI investors already hold indirect exposure through SoftBank's Vision Fund, mutual funds with Nvidia positions, or direct stakes in companies building on GPT-4 and Claude APIs.

The question is whether $3.5 trillion in combined valuations for three companies — none of which is profitable — can withstand the current macro headwinds: oil near $97, a possible Fed rate hike by October, and global bond yields at multi-year highs.

Gil Luria of D.A. Davidson put it bluntly: "What OpenAI does not want is for the public market capital to exhaust itself."

*Sources: Reuters, Wall Street Journal, MarketWatch, CNBC, Financial Times*
